entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Juan Negrín López was a Spanish physician and politician who served as prime minister of the Second Spanish Republic. He was a leader of the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party and of the left-leaning Popular Front government during the Spanish Civil War. He also served as minister of finance and minister of defence. He was the last Republican premier of Spain (1937–1939), leading the government forces defeated by the Nationalists under General Francisco Franco. He went into exile in Paris, France, where he served as prime minister of the Spanish Republican government in exile until 1945, when he was replaced by José Giral.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Juan Negrín's leadership of the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party and the Popular Front government during the Spanish Civil War had significant regional impact, with his defeat leading to the rise of General Francisco Franco and a long period of authoritarian rule in Spain. His exile and continued leadership of the Republican government in Paris played a role in shaping the post-war international landscape.
